# sandhi

> Any AI you choose marks your story's structure, in your own words. It never writes a sentence. One static file, no account.

sandhi is a single-page tool for writers at https://sandhi.naklitechie.com. You write a story on the Story Spine (beats with a fortune, phase, joint word and the principles each serves), or paste prose and let a model you choose mark its beats, turn, low point, joints and threads. The model only labels; every beat is the writer's own text, cut where the model's exact quote lands. Checks compare labels: empty or idle beats, slack joints ("and then"), plants that never pay off, payoffs with no plant, luck after the turn.

## Agent face
- `window.sandhi` (and `navigator.modelContext` tools named `sandhi.<tool>` where the browser has it): 49 tools over one command bus. Start with `status`. `story.start` builds a story from Story Spine lines, as the New-story wizard does; `read.paragraphs` stages prose split by paragraph for the writer to accept; `story.recent` lists the stories a replace pushed aside; `story.sketch` sets the fortune shape the writer wants; `tidbit.add`, `tidbit.update` and `tidbit.remove` keep real-life observations and place them in beats; `thread.update {open: true}` leaves a plant open on purpose; `write.questions`, `write.options`, `write.joints`, `write.shape`, `write.place`, `write.plot`, `write.interview` and `write.depth` ask the chosen reader about a beat or the joints, and nothing they return enters the story. Mutations are undoable. `read.accept`, `write.apply` and `reader.key` are person-only. An agent reads on the device, or on the writer's provider only when the writer chose it.
- Outcome envelope: `{ok, class, data?, message?, next?}`; classes are a closed list (see SPEC.md §0).

## Readers (the AI ladder)
- A model server on this machine: Ollama (127.0.0.1:11434) or LM Studio (127.0.0.1:1234).
- Gemini Nano in Chrome (Prompt API); a preview, below the quality floor in tests.
- The writer's provider and key: OpenRouter, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, Groq, Mistral, DeepSeek, Together, or any OpenAI-compatible URL. Keys stay in the browser's IndexedDB.
